review_mode: Statement-only blind; no author proof or other referee report read.
mathematical_verdict: PROVED under frozen assumptions and cited standard polynomial-bit normal-form theorem. No statement repair recommended.
source_qualification: Milne relevant full text verified. Kannan–Bachem polynomial-bit theorem confirmed from authoritative publisher abstract; full paper not retrievable and its internal proof not independently audited.

findings.claim: Eligible 2-primary exponent a is in {1,2}; J+mR is precisely the odd part and a*J_o is contained in J.
Odd H-invariant ideals descend without ramification obstruction; d_H^h=D_o, including arbitrary odd composite support.
Signed invariant basis is integral, disjoint-support, and rank n/h; inconsistent signed components vanish.
Ordinary-basis quantities and all subfield contraction indices are polynomial-bit computable; square nonsingular HNF suffices.
findings.qualification: Standard normal-form complexity import as disclosed.

findings.claim: Binary collision search acquires the short multiplier with polynomial numeric-index cost; rounding/division is exact under the strict guard.
The actual inherited width guard implies r<1/(8192*n^4)<1/(4*sqrt(n)) for every allowed finite n.
Bounded prime support and polynomial exponent imply log2 d_g<=rho*g+2*t*C*log2 n; a logarithmic power-of-two g suffices asymptotically.
Finite small dimensions are legitimately absorbed, with all basis/target/output lengths still charged.

negative_controls: Ramified ideal (1-i) violates d^h=D if odd-part separation is omitted.
Rounding at exact coefficient error +1/2 can fail; strict guard retained.
Eligible trivial-stabilizer examples with p=257 and growing finite support can require only g=n; finite evidence is not an infinite-family lower bound.
scope: No source-hardness, fixed-family reduction, ordinary-input-basis acquisition for an external reduction, or probabilistic DD theorem follows from this review. Same-model scrutiny is correlated.
